1.explanation: In components/prism-typescript.js, the call Prism.languages.typescript.keyword.push(...) injects a regex to recognize TS‐only keywords (including “infer” and “type”). The regex uses a loose negative lookahead that fails to enforce proper word boundaries, so it matches prefixes of longer identifiers (e.g. “inference”, “typeDefs”). This is the root cause of the over‐eager highlighting. Editing this regex in the keyword.push call—replacing it with one that demands a true word boundary after the keyword—will prevent partial matches and fix the bug.
1.bug_scenario: The screenshots illustrate import statements in a TSX file where Prism’s TypeScript highlighter treats “infer” and “type” as standalone keywords even when they are part of longer identifiers. For example, in “import { infer, inference, infer }…”, “inference” is wrongly flagged as a keyword. Likewise, “typeDefs” in “import { type, typeDefs, type }…” is also highlighted as if it were the bare “type” keyword. By contrast, “const” and “constants” behave correctly.

2.explanation: The root of the problem lies in the regex pushed onto Prism.languages.typescript.keyword. The pattern `/\b(?:asserts|infer|interface|module|namespace|type)(?!\s*[^\s_${}*a-zA-Z\xA0-\uFFFF])/` is intended to match only standalone keywords followed by whitespace or punctuation. However, its negative lookahead is too permissive and still matches when the keyword is immediately followed by alphabetic characters, so “inference” and “typeDefs” are wrongly highlighted. Adjusting this regex (for example by enforcing a word boundary after the keyword) in the call to `Prism.languages.typescript.keyword.push` will correct the behavior.
2.bug_scenario: In TSX/TypeScript imports, the highlighter treats keywords like “infer” and “type” as keywords even when they’re part of longer identifiers (e.g. “inference”, “typeDefs”), causing incorrect highlighting on “inference” and “typeDefs” while correctly leaving “constants” alone.
